package_info.why_malicious: The package contains an XSS vulnerability due to insufficient sanitization of user-supplied Markdown input, allowing attackers to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript via crafted links. This enables cross-site scripting attacks when user input is rendered as HTML.

execution_context.file_location: application code using marked to render user input (e.g., in Goof's note rendering logic)
required_permissions: network (if exfiltration is attempted via XSS)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user input is rendered, the code injects a Markdown link with a crafted href using 'javascript&#58this;alert(1)'. The marked package fails to sanitize this input, resulting in an HTML anchor tag with an href that browsers interpret as executable JavaScript, leading to XSS when a user clicks the link.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This input is designed to bypass sanitization by encoding the colon as '&#58', which the browser decodes, allowing JavaScript execution via a link.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Markdown rendering libraries are expected to sanitize or remove dangerous protocols like 'javascript:' in links, especially when the sanitize option is enabled. Here, the sanitizer fails to recognize the encoded colon, allowing the attack.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate Markdown links should only use safe protocols (http, https, mailto, etc.) and should not allow JavaScript execution.
key_indicators: Presence of 'javascript:' or encoded variants in link hrefs
Use of HTML entities to obfuscate dangerous protocols
Sanitizer fails to remove or encode the malicious link

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a crafted Markdown link with an obfuscated JavaScript protocol (e.g., [Gotcha](javascript&#58this;alert(1))) as user input.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious link is stored and later rendered by the application.

attack_chain.action: Application uses marked to render the Markdown input to HTML with sanitize option enabled, but the sanitizer fails to detect the obfuscated JavaScript protocol.
attack_chain.leads_to: HTML output contains an <a> tag with a dangerous href.

attack_chain.action: User views the rendered content and clicks the malicious link, causing the browser to execute the JavaScript payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: XSS is triggered, allowing attacker-controlled JavaScript execution in the victim's browser.

behavioral_signatures: Markdown links with hrefs containing 'javascript:' or encoded variants (e.g., 'javascript:')
HTML output from Markdown rendering containing <a> tags with href attributes starting with 'javascript:' or entity-encoded equivalents
User input containing suspicious HTML entities in link protocols
file_indicators: User-supplied Markdown content with [text](javascript:...) or [text](javascript:...) patterns
HTML output with <a href="javascript:..."> or <a href="javascript:...">
network_indicators: Unusual outbound requests triggered by user interaction with rendered links (if XSS payloads exfiltrate data)
Browser requests to attacker-controlled domains after clicking links in user-generated content
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan rendered HTML for anchor tags with href attributes that begin with 'javascript:' or any HTML entity-encoded variant (e.g., 'javascript:'). Additionally, monitor user input for Markdown links containing suspicious protocols or encoded characters. Implement or verify that the Markdown renderer's sanitizer correctly decodes and blocks all forms of 'javascript:' links, including those obfuscated with HTML entities.
